description: Add Network Status panel to dashboard.html UI, implement frontend /api/network polling, add stream status indicator (LIVE/OFFLINE), and handle RTMP disconnections gracefully with visual state.
steps: In templates/dashboard.html: Add a 'Network Status' panel inside the live-detection section (between the threshold slider area and the analysis panel, or as a sub-panel within the live feed panel). The panel should display: (a) PC IP address (host_ip from /api/network), (b) DJI RTMP Address (rtmp_address), (c) Stream Key (stream_key). Add a stream status indicator (LIVE/OFFLINE badge) next to or replacing the existing live-indicator-text 'DRONE POV'. The indicator should show green 'LIVE' when camera_connected is true, red 'OFFLINE' when false.

In static/js/dashboard.js: (a) Add a new poll function pollNetwork() that calls GET /api/network every 10 seconds (10000ms). On success, update the Network Status panel elements with host_ip, rtmp_address, stream_key. (b) Update the existing applyStatus() function to set the stream status indicator based on camera_connected. When camera_connected changes from true to false, show OFFLINE state gracefully (no page crash, keep polling). When it changes back, show LIVE. (c) Wire pollNetwork() into the init() function with setInterval.

In static/style.css: Add styles for the network-status-panel (consistent with existing dark theme card style using var(--card-bg), var(--card-border), var(--radius)). Style the LIVE/OFFLINE indicator (green dot + text for LIVE, red dot + text for OFFLINE). Ensure responsive layout on mobile.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard HTML contains a Network Status panel with elements for host_ip, rtmp_address, stream_key display
Frontend polls /api/network every 10 seconds and updates the panel dynamically
Stream status shows LIVE (green) when camera_connected is true from /status
Stream status shows OFFLINE (red) when camera_connected is false
RTMP disconnection is handled gracefully - UI shows OFFLINE state and auto-recovers when reconnected
All existing dashboard functionality preserved (alert banner, audio, crack analysis, threshold slider, WebRTC iframe)
verification: Run: python -c "from app import app; c = app.test_client(); r = c.get('/'); assert b'network-status' in r.data or b'networkStatus' in r.data; assert b'/api/network' in r.data or b'api/network' in r.data; print('Dashboard has network panel')"
Run: python tests/test_integration.py and confirm all tests pass including the dashboard content assertions
findings: All integration tests pass. The /api/network reference is in the separate dashboard.js file (loaded via script tag), not inline in the HTML. The HTML contains network-status-panel, networkStatusPanel, streamStatusBadge IDs. Verification using the briefing command (checking for network-status in r.data) passes correctly.
